main_text.l: altera vicis rarior, quos ix tantum habet, palustri fere, & passim humili ac vliginoso solo, in australem priorem sequens, ad interiora vergens, per quam ab ortu venientibus iter Groningam est: eam Duerswoldiam proprio nomine appellitant. Atq; hactenus quidem populi hujus regionis, quos jam quidam inepte velut proprio & peculiari horum nomine, ac vocabulo absolute VMLANDOS nuncupant, & nuncupari debere contendunt, cum certius nihil notiusve sit ex etymi ratione, & exemplis in literarum monumentis, quam vocabulum id appellativum aut commune esse, & in genere τῶν πρὸς τι referendum ad urbem aut locum aliquem celebrem, circum quem ager populive siti sunt; atq; hos ipsos populos sic dictos, quod positu suo Groningam fere circum veniant. Unde ista in antiquiorib. literis, adeoq; nuperis etiam ante inventum hoc litis ergo σοφὸν φάρμακον, Die Omblanden bp Groningen / bin Groningen / ban Groningen: quemadmodum alibi, die Omblanden / bin offte bp Franeker / Wolstwerdt / Leiwerden & similia: Item Groningen mit ere bimlanden / vt Dcko thom Wlaoech / Sibet tho Susttringen mit ehre bimblanden.

Sed quo abeo? ad rem revertor. Omnes hi populi, quos ja recensui, in tres partes, ceu membra regionis, hodie divisi sunt, & dudum divisi fuere: quarum prima, qua trans Hunesum ad occidentem & meridiem est, usq; in Lavicam & Ostergoos, ac occidentalis vulgo nuncupatur: altera Hunesgomes eis Hunesum, tertia Fivelgonios comple-

page.notes: Marginal notes: "Iterum de nomine regionis." (right, beside "nuncupari debere"); "Litere in publica forma extant cum sigillis." (right, beside "Unde ista"); "Tripartita eorum qui se Vinlandos vocant, divisio." (right, beside "quarum prima"). The three right-margin notes are printed in small type and are transcribed here as their own notes at the nearest position; the note beside "Unde ista" and the one beside "quarum prima" were not placed in the text above and should be inserted at those positions when the page is assembled. Greek "σοφὸν φάρμακον" is a doubtful reading of a damaged word and may be "ἀσοφὸν" [?]. The Greek "τῶν πρὸς τι" is printed with a tilde-like mark that may be misread. "Groningam" is printed as is, with the m-form of the place name. Black-letter German words are marked with bl. Long s has been read as plain s throughout (e.g. "Hunesum"). The catchword "Ettur," stands at the right below the last line.
